rules.name: RedHat.ConsciousLanguage
rules.message: Use %s rather than '%s'.

rules.name: RedHat.Contractions
rules.message: Avoid contractions. Use '%s' rather than '%s.'

rules.name: RedHat.Definitions
rules.message: Define acronyms and abbreviations (such as '%s') on first occurrence if they're likely to be unfamiliar.

rules.name: RedHat.DoNotUseTerms
rules.message: %s
swap: Do not use "ACK" as acronym for "acknowledgement". When writing about the acknowledgement flag ("ACK flag") or acknowledgement packet ("ACK packet") in a TCP packet, use "ACK flag" or "ACK packet".
Do not use "future-proof" in a statement about the benefits, characteristics, or performance of a Red Hat product or service.'
Do not use "out of the box" or "out-of-the-box". Use text that is suitable for the context and the noun to which this adjective applies.
Do not use "and/or". Depending on the context, use one of the following constructions: a and b, a or b, or a, b, or both.
Do not use "basically". "Basically" is another term for "in principle" or "fundamentally".
Do not use "congratulations" in technical information."
Do not use "debuggable". Rephrase the sentence to use the verb or noun debug. For example, change rebuild the debuggable version to rebuild the version that can be debugged.
Do not use "foo". This term is technical jargon in code and as shorthand for fubar, an acronym of profanity in code.
Do not use "fubar". This term is an acronym of a profanity that is sometimes used by developers in code.
Do not use colors to describe something unless it is also described non-visually, for example, with the name of the item.
Do not use "kerberize" to refer to applications or services that use Kerberos authentication. Refer to such applications as "Kerberos-aware" or "Kerberos-enabled", or rewrite the sentence.
Do not use "native interface" to refer to the command line interface for the JBoss EAP management tool.
Do not use "overhead". Use terminology that is more specific. For example, write "running large queries can increase processor usage".
Do not use "please" in technical documentation.
Do not use "quiescent". If a system is, or needs to be inactive, write "inactive". If a system is, or needs to be safe, write "safe".
Do not use "resides" if a simpler verb is possible.
Do not use "respective" or "respectively". Rewrite to avoid using these words.
Do not use "time-tested". Time-tested implies a claim of suitability or reliability.

rules.name: RedHat.Ellipses
rules.message: Avoid the ellipsis (...) except to indicate omitted words.

rules.name: RedHat.EmDash
rules.message: Do not use em dashes. Use punctuation marks such as commas, parentheses, or colons instead.

rules.name: RedHat.GitLinks
rules.message: Do not include a link to %s unless it is explicitly approved.

rules.name: RedHat.HeadingPunctuation
rules.message: Do not use end punctuation in headings.

rules.name: RedHat.Headings
rules.message: Use sentence-style capitalization in '%s'.
exceptions: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes

rules.name: RedHat.Hyphens
rules.message: Use %s rather than '%s'.

rules.name: RedHat.MergeConflictMarkers
rules.message: Do not commit Git merge conflict markers in source code.

rules.name: RedHat.NoGerundsInTitles
rules.message: Where possible, avoid using gerunds in topic titles. Use the imperative form instead.

rules.name: RedHat.ObviousTerms
rules.message: Consider not documenting %s because it is self-explanatory.

rules.name: RedHat.OxfordComma
rules.message: Use the Oxford comma in '%s'.

rules.name: RedHat.PassiveVoice
rules.message: '%s' is passive voice. In general, use active voice. Consult the style guide for acceptable use of passive voice.

rules.name: RedHat.ProductCentricWriting
rules.message: Do not use transitive verb constructions like '%s' to grant abilities to inanimate objects. Whenever possible, use direct, user-focused sentences where the subject of the sentence performs the action.

rules.name: RedHat.ReleaseNotes
rules.message: For release notes, consider using '%s' rather than '%s'.

rules.name: RedHat.RepeatedWords
rules.message: '%s' is repeated.

rules.name: RedHat.SelfReferentialText
rules.message: Avoid using self-referential text such as '%s'.

rules.name: RedHat.SentenceLength
rules.message: Try to keep sentences to an average of 32 words or fewer.

rules.name: RedHat.SessionId
rules.message: Do not publish URLs that contain session identifiers. Exposed session IDs enable session hijacking and unauthorized account access.

rules.name: RedHat.SimpleWords
rules.message: Use simple language. Consider using '%s' rather than '%s'.

rules.name: RedHat.SmartQuotes
rules.message: Do not use smart quotation marks. Use %s rather than %s.

rules.name: RedHat.Spacing
rules.message: Keep one space between words in '%s'.

rules.name: RedHat.Symbols
rules.message: Do not use the '%s' symbol.
